body:
## Proposed change

The newer Platin hubs, the Stereo Hub HT and the Surround Hub, are built on Libre's LS10 module. Their SSDP description matches the LibreSync matchers and their control port answers, so 2026.11 discovers them and lets the user add them. But their port 7777 does not accept the integration's plaintext session (on the Surround Hub it is TLS with a client certificate), so `async_connect` never succeeds and the entry stays in "retrying setup" for ever.

This PR tells the two generations apart before connecting. aiolibresync 0.5.2 adds `async_query_lssdp`, which asks the hub on Libre's own discovery port (UDP 1800), and the reply names the module: `LS9` on the original Stereo Hub, `LS10` on the newer ones.

- Both config flows abort with `unsupported_hub` when the hub reports LS10.
- An entry added with 2026.11 on such a hub fails setup with a translated `ConfigEntryError` instead of retrying.
- The LSSDP query runs alongside the connection in setup and alongside the probe in the flows, so a hub that is down, or a mistyped address, waits no longer than before.
- A hub that does not answer on LSSDP is treated as unknown and handled as before.

This refusal is a stopgap, not the end state for these hubs. We are working with owners of both models to add support (drsound/ha-libresync#2 for the Stereo Hub HT, drsound/ha-libresync#3 for the Surround Hub). They have captured and tested the control protocol on their own hubs, and from their findings the companion custom integration has beta builds that run the LS10 hubs on port 50006 alone (source and power), now waiting for the owners to confirm them on their hardware. Once confirmed, that support will come to core as a follow-up PR, and the full feature set will follow as port 7777 over TLS is worked out with them.
